text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Chelsea and Burnley at Stamford Bridge!
Chelsea still have an outside chance of booking a place in Europe next season, and a win here could move them into the top half of the table if results around them also go their way.

The Blues are unbeaten in their four outings in all competitions since losing the EFL Cup final to Liverpool (W3 D1) and booked another trip to Wembley last time out as they beat Leicester City 4-2 to reach the FA Cup semi-final.
Their home form is good too, having lost just one of their last 14 games at Stamford Bridge in all competitions (W10 D3).
Burnley got their first win since before Christmas before the international break, beating 10-man Brentford 2-1 to end an 11-match winless run in all competitions (D3 L8).
The Clarets are still five points below Luton Town in 17th place, but another win here would certainly give them a boost in the relegation fight.

However, Burnley are one of three teams yet to win successive Premier League games this season (along with Crystal Palace and Sheffield United), and they haven't done so since April 2022, when they managed three in a row.
Mauricio Pochettino makes three changes to the side that beat Leicester in the FA Cup before the international break.
Petrovic is back in goal, with Badiashile and Fernandez also coming in.
Gusto has recovered from illness to retain his place, but Sterling drops to the bench.
There are more injury troubles for the Blues as well, as Robert Sanchez, Trevoh Chalobah and Ben Chilwell have all picked up problems which keep them out today.
Vincent Kompany makes just two changes from the Clarets' win over Brentford two weeks ago.
Amdouni and Foster are brought in to play together up front, while Odobert and Vitinho both drop back into deeper roles.
Taylor starts on the bench, but in-form David Datro Fofana isn't available today as he's ineligible to face his parent club.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Bruun Larsen gets the game under way for Burnley!
CHANCE! Chelsea are looking to make a quick start to this game, and Gallagher spreads it out to Palmer on the left.
He has options in the middle, but chooses to go it alone instead, firing his shot into the side netting.
It's a positive run down the left by Odobert as he weaves between Chelsea players before pulling it back from the byline.
Disasi scuffs it away, but the Blues only get to the halfway line before losing possession.
Chelsea are a bit sluggish in defence, and Gallagher trips Cullen to give away a free-kick through the middle.
Bruun Larsen takes it, but his shot is straight at the wall, and it deflects out for a corner.
Berge wants it more than Mudryk, and though Chelsea want a free-kick, the midfielder won it cleanly.
Burnley have another chance to push forward, but Vitinho's throughball is too heavy for Odobert.
WIDE! Seconds after Bruun Larsen bundled a shot wide, it's switched back out to the Dane on the right of the box.
The angle is against him though, and he fizzes his low effort just wide of the far post.
GREAT SAVE! Chelsea finally manage to string together enough passes to get to the edge of the box, and Gallagher squares it across to Fernandez.
His shot takes an awkward deflection off Esteve, but Muric adjusts quickly to tip it onto the bar.
WIDE! Amdouni is caught on the ball by Caicedo, and the midfielder rolls it into Palmer's feet.
He isn't short on confidence as he takes on another pacy shot from range, but he fires this one wide of the near post.
CHANCE! Palmer is causing all sorts of problems in the opening exchanges here, as he plays a one-two with Gallagher to open up space on the right of the box.
He doesn't hit the shot cleanly though, hitting it wide of the near post once more.
GOOD SAVE! Just like Palmer, Odobert has been bright so far, and he cuts inside from the left.
As Gusto closes him down, the winger uses him as a shield to curl a shot towards the far post, but Petrovic gets a strong hand to it.
Mudryk loses Amdouni with a drop of the shoulder, forcing Assignon to cover.
He tugs the Ukrainian back by his shoulder and earns the first booking of the game.
BLOCK! It's a great throughball down the right by Caicedo, and Gusto surges down the wing to meet it.
He pulls it back to Palmer, who hits his shot first time, but O'Shea makes sure he's in the way of it.
GREAT SAVE! Chelsea work it wonderfully down their right side again, and this time, Palmer tries to turn provider.
He threads it through to Jackson, who hits his low shot across goal towards the far post, but Muric stays big, making a big block with his foot.
DISASI SCORES! The corner was taken short to Mudryk, and he whips a dangerous cross in from the left.
Berge gets the deftest of touches at the near post, but can only help it onto Disasi, who bundles it over the line from close range.
There is a VAR check though, and this might not count...
The initial VAR check was to see if Mudryk was offside, but once that's cleared, they look to see if the final touch by Disasi was off his arm.
He ducked his head to try and head it, but it does look like the ball went in off his elbow.
NO GOAL! After a very long look at the goal from all angles, it appears that Disasi didn't get his head to the ball, and as it came off his line, the goal will be ruled out.
Still 0-0!
Chelsea push forward in numbers once more, and the space just opens up for Gallagher through the middle.
A deflection off O'Shea takes it neatly into Muric's gloves, and Palmer is furious, as he was completely unmarked to his right.
SAVE! Chelsea don't deal with Assignon's long throw into the box, and it bounces out to Cullen on the edge of the D.
He quickly adjusts himself to shoot, drilling a low effort through the crowd, but Petrovic gets down to hold onto it.
Burnley have really struggled to deal with the threat that Chelsea are posing down their right.
Gusto drives to the byline before pulling it back to Jackson, who can't sort his feet out quickly enough to have a shot.
Chelsea have scored at least once in all 17 of their previous Premier League games against Burnley, the most they've ever faced a side while scoring 100 per cent of the time in the competition.
Cucurella is looking for a forward pass, but there's no movement ahead of him.
Assignon quickly closes him down, and Chelsea are forced all the way back to the goalkeeper, much to the fans' frustration.
SAVE! It's a hopeful clearance upfield, but Jackson latches onto it with a bursting run down the right.
He cuts inside to lose Vitinho before laying it off to Mudryk, but he tries to guide it into the net, leaving Muric with a comfortable save.
Cucurella steps across Assignon to block his run, and though there isn't a lot of contact, the Spaniard knew what he was doing.
He gives away a free-kick, and gets a booking.
Petrovic makes an easy save from Bruun Larsen's free-kick and sends it long upfield.
Jackson races out to the left to meet it, with Muric also rushing out of his box.
The forward just gets there first, but the goalkeeper recovers well to poke it away for a corner.
CHANCE! Palmer's throughball is just too heavy for Caicedo, but it runs out to Gusto on the right.
He fizzes a low cross into the middle, and Cucurella throws himself forward to meet it with his head.
It's straight at Muric though.
PENALTY TO CHELSEA! Mudryk is racing onto a throughball into the box, and Assignon gets back into position.
The ball gets away from the Ukrainian, and the defender puts his arm on Mudryk's shoulder to nudge him down.
The referee points to the spot!
ASSIGNON IS OFF! The Frenchman was booked early on in this game, and that challenge for the penalty is deemed to be his second bookable offence.
After pointing to the spot, the referee goes to his pocket to pull out a second yellow card for Assignon, who is sent off, much to Burnley's disbelief.
Burnley are down to 10!
VAR has a long look at the penalty incident, but they don't see anything wrong with the referee's onfield decision.
The penalty stands, but Assignon is still refusing to leave the pitch.
KOMPANY IS SENT OFF! The Burnley manager is not happy with the penalty and red card decisions, and he is making that point first to the fourth official and then to the referee.
He crosses a line with his protests, and he is also shown a red card, much to the home fans' amusement.

PALMER SCORES! He had to wait a long time to take it, but that didn't faze him in the least! It's as cool as you like from Palmer, who steps up to the spot and dinks a lovely Panenka penalty straight down the middle while Muric dives to his left.
1-0 Chelsea!
Burnley are forced into a change now, and they're going to sacrifice one of their forwards for another defender.
Amdouni is taken off, with Taylor coming on to slot in at right-back.
Gallagher has already got away with a couple of fouls in this game, and this time, he gets a booking.
He stretches for the ball, but catches Taylor instead, and the referee goes to his pocket.
The board has now gone up to show that we're in seven minutes of stoppage time at the end of the half.
Burnley have a free-kick that Bruun Larsen curls into the far post, but Esteve nods it across goal and wide.
The yellow card is out again, this time for Cullen, who goes through the back of Caicedo, catching him with the follow-through.
Burnley are sitting deeper than they were earlier in the game, allowing Chelsea to keep possession in front of them.
The Blues are staying patient though, trying to draw them out.
GOOD SAVE! Gusto has shown a real threat down the right all game so far, and he advances forward from right-back once more.
He takes on a shot himself this time, but Muric makes himself big to smother it.
HALF-TIME: CHELSEA 1-0 BURNLEY.
Palmer's penalty separates the sides at the break, with Chelsea beating 10-man Burnley 1-0.
The Blues were dominant in the first half, and they thought they'd taken the lead through Disasi 20 minutes in, but the goal was disallowed as it went in off his elbow.
Muric made some great saves to deny Fernandez and Jackson before things went downhill for Burnley.
Assignon brought down Mudryk in the box, and the referee pointed to the spot and gave the Frenchman his second yellow of the game.
Kompany was also sent off for dissent before Palmer scored a wonderful Panenka penalty to put his side in front.
Despite a slightly slow start, Pochettino will be pleased with what he's seen from his side.
They created an xG (expected goals) of 2.33 from their 16 shots, seven of which were on target, and they look likely to add more to their tally after the break.
Burnley had a couple of bright moments but only managed an xG of 0.48 from their 10 shots.
Petrovic made a couple of comfortable saves, but this could be a long second half for the 10-man Clarets.
There's another change for Burnley at the break, as Bruun Larsen is taken off for Brownhill.
Chelsea get us back under way for the second half!
CULLEN EQUALISES! What a start to the second half for Burnley! That will be exactly what Kompany was looking for as Vitinho works it inside from the right, squaring a pacy cross to Brownhill.
The substitute stretches to cushion it down for Cullen, who hits it first time with the outside of his right boot, firing it past Petrovic and into the back of the net.
It looked like it was going to get away from Brownhill, but he did well to adjust himself so that he could bring it down, bouncing it to Cullen's feet.
That goal has silenced the home crowd, and Chelsea are working to try and change that.
They look to Gusto on the right once more, but he can't get away from Taylor this time.

Palmer is the fifth player to reach 20 goal involvements in his first Premier League season with Chelsea after Jimmy-Floyd Hasselbaink (32 in 2000-01), Eden Hazard (20 in 2012-13), Diego Costa (23 in 2014-15) and Cesc Fabregas (21 in 2014-15).
Chelsea are back to dominating possession here, but it's all in front of a compact Burnley side.
The Blues are staying patient, but there's no space to work in at the moment.
There's been just one shot in the second half so far, which obviously became Burnley's equaliser.
Cullen scored from an xG of just 0.03, and Chelsea haven't managed a reply just yet.
Fernandez's throughball takes a big deflection and Burnley are static until Mudryk touches it.
O'Shea slides in to stop him from having a shot before Chelsea recycle it out to Gusto.
His first touch is poor though, and Taylor sees it back to Muric.
GREAT SAVE! Burnley could've been in front! Cullen peels out to the left this time and looks to turn provider as he whips a dangerous cross to the edge of the six-yard box.
Foster gets goalside of Badiashile to thump a header on goal, but Petrovic gets behind it.
BLOCK! Gallagher weaves past two Burnley defenders before touching it back to Mudryk, who loses O'Shea with a clever dummy.
He takes the shot on after, but Esteve throws himself in front of it to make a vital block.
Chelsea are making their first change of the game now.
Gallagher hands Fernandez the captain's armband as he makes his way off.
Madueke comes on for him.
GREAT SAVE! Chelsea have found their first-half rhythm again now, and Mudryk makes another brilliant run down the left.
He pulls it back from the byline to Jackson, but Muric makes himself big to block the first-time shot.
After struggling against Gusto down the left in the first half, Vitinho is now have a hard time keeping up with Mudryk after switching to the opposite flank.
The Ukrainian gets away again, but the shot at the end of the run is poor.
Chelsea have had 79.2 per cent of the possession in the second half so far, and they're still keeping Burnley penned back deep.
The Clarets are still standing firm though, even as the pressure increases.
SAVE! Chelsea just about clear their lines after a Burnley free-kick, and Mudryk surges forward on the counter.
He lays it off to Madueke on the edge of the D, but his low shot is straight at Muric.

source.text: He lays it off to Madueke

text: Burnley are making a double change this time.
Foster, who could easily have put Burnley ahead in this game with his header, goes off for Rodriguez.
And Odobert, who has been a lot quieter in the second half after a bright first 45 minutes, goes off for Gudmundsson.
WHAT A CHANCE! Fernandez lifts a long pass over the top to Madueke, and he can only touch it into Gusto's path.
He drills an inviting ball across the face of goal, and Jackson directs his first-time shot back across goal and wide.
Second change for Chelsea now, and it's Sterling that's coming on in place of Caicedo.
SAVE! Muric is keeping his side in the game here as he stops another Chelsea attack.
Cucurella pulls it back to Palmer on the edge of the D, but his pacy shot is held by the goalkeeper at the near bottom corner.
Craig Bellamy is screaming instructions on the sidelines as he tries to organise his team.
Chelsea are finding more space in behind, and the Burnley coach is trying to close them before they're punished.
PALMER SCORES AGAIN! Fernandez slides it forward for Sterling, and he plays a lovely backheel straight into Palmer's feet.
The youngster gets between the two Burnley centre-backs and fires his second goal of the game into the bottom-right corner to put Chelsea back in front.
2-1 to the hosts!
It's a wonderful piece of skill by Sterling, who didn't have many options with his back to goal but executed the backheel flick perfectly.
Burnley win another free-kick on the left, and Cullen floats a great cross into the far post.
Rodriguez goes to attack it, but Madueke just manages to shepherd it out for a corner.
O'SHEA EQUALISES! Burnley are level again! The Clarets are refusing to go down without a fight, and it's a lovely whipped corner into the box by Cullen.
O'Shea runs to the near post and has a free header as he thumps it across goal.
Petrovic gets two hands to it, but can't stop it from hitting the back of the net.
Cullen's brilliant delivery from the free-kick won them the corner, and from that set-piece, he picks out O'Shea for the equaliser.
WIDE! Sterling switches it out to Madueke on the right of the box, and he drops a shoulder to lose Esteve.
He drags at his shot though, and it rolls just wide of Muric's near post.
WHAT A MISS! Cullen is reluctant to close Palmer down, and he's able to pick out another wonderful cross.
Sterling peels away from his defender to get a free header, and when it looks easier to score, he sends his header wide of the far post.
Gusto pulls up with a hamstring problem, and it looks like his name is going to be added to Chelsea's long injury list.
He's taken off, with Gilchrist coming on to replace him.
OFF THE BAR! Chelsea are all over the place during another Burnley corner, and Rodriguez rises high above everybody to power a header at goal.
Petrovic is beaten, but it smacks the bar, and the substitute can only volley his follow-up effort well wide.
It's end-to-end at the minute as both sides push for a winner late on.
Palmer, unsurprisingly, is at the centre of it all for Chelsea again, but when he slides it forward for Madueke, Muric reacts quickest to cut out the pass.
We're into the first of five additional minutes here, and Muric is trying to take his time over a clearance.
He knows he can't take too long, and when he does throw it upfield, Rodriguez wins a free-kick.
Esteve dawdles over a free-kick, and he's booked for time-wasting.
Cullen can only delay the Chelsea attack when it gets caught under his feet, but the Blues win it back before spreading it to Madueke on the right.
Taylor stands his ground to give away a corner, but Burnley just about clear their lines.
FULL-TIME: CHELSEA 2-2 BURNLEY.
10-man Burnley come from behind twice to earn a point in a 2-2 draw with Chelsea.
The Blues dominated the first half, and Disasi had a goal ruled out by VAR for handball before Palmer gave them the lead.

Mudryk was brought down in the box by Assignon, and the referee pointed to the spot before sending the Frenchman off for his second booking, which was quickly followed by a red card for Kompany for dissent.
Palmer scored a wonderful Panenka from the spot to put them in front, but Burnley pulled level just two minutes after the break through Cullen's long-range strike.
Muric made vital saves to keep his side in it before Palmer eventually got his second of the game with a drilled finish, but just three minutes later, O'Shea thumped in an equaliser.
Sterling missed a sitter, while Rodriguez struck the bar as both teams searched for a winner, but there was nothing to separate the sides.
Chelsea went off to boos from the home fans and now turn their attention to Manchester United on Thursday as they stay in 11th.
Burnley are still 19th but are now four points from safety.
They host Wolves on Tuesday.
That's all for today, goodbye!
